02

Three Problems for Program Owners

I

Your Assurer May Report to Your Supplier.

Where the integrator, the cloud platform and the security provider sit inside one group, an internal assurance opinion cannot resolve the conflict however good the people are. Check the last opinion your program received and follow the reporting line up.

II

Accreditation Is About to Filter Your Supply Chain.

As NCAP rolls out during 2026, providers serving critical infrastructure will need UAE accreditation. Run your supplier list against that requirement now, and note how many of the names you depend on you cannot answer for.

III

The Cryptographic Mandate Lands on Government First.

Migration-plan submission during 2026 applies to government entities ahead of the wider market, and the plan has to rest on an inventory. Most organizations do not have one. Ask whether yours is a document or an assumption.

04

Common Questions

How does Orvix contract with a government entity?

Through accredited local partners who hold the contract with the entity. Orvix works inside the program as the independent assessor and engineering team.

What is the National Cyber Accreditation Programme?

A UAE program rolling out during 2026 that restricts which cybersecurity providers may serve critical infrastructure.

What is NESA IAS v2 and who does it apply to?

The federal baseline of 188 controls, 39 of them mandatory Priority One, applying to government entities, CNI operators and their IT suppliers.

Why use an external assessor when we already have an integrator?

Because an integrator reports on the program it is delivering, while an assessor reports on whether that program's controls can be evidenced to a third party.

Who performs work that requires security clearance?

The accredited partner’s cleared staff, working to Orvix’s method. Our own team carries out the assessment and engineering work around them, remotely and on site as the program needs.
